findings.issue: IsSequenceRaceException (line 210) classifies ANY DbUpdateException whose inner SqliteException has primary code 19 as a (kind, year) insert race — it never checks WHICH entity failed, nor the extended code. SQLITE_CONSTRAINT 19 also covers NOT NULL (1299), FOREIGN KEY (787) and CHECK (1811), and this class's own XML doc (lines 25-27) states that its SaveChangesAsync 'flushes every other tracked change on that context' — i.e. the caller's correspondence/attachment rows, inside the caller's transaction. So an unrelated constraint failure on another tracked entity is now swallowed as a race. Worse, the recovery then breaks: I verified empirically (EF Core 10.0.12 + Microsoft.Data.Sqlite probe) that ReloadAsync on an Added entry whose row is NOT in the store leaves the entry in state Added (it does not detach), so on the next loop iteration FirstOrDefaultAsync returns null (the query hits the DB and finds nothing), the code takes the `row is null` branch and calls db.OfficialNumbers.Add(new OfficialNumber{...}) — which throws InvalidOperationException: "The instance of entity type 'OfficialNumber' cannot be tracked because another instance with the same key value for {'Kind','Year'} is already being tracked". That throw is OUTSIDE the try, so it is neither retried nor mapped, it is raw English EF text, and the real SqliteException (the actual cause the user needs) is dropped from the exception chain entirely. This is a regression: before this package the same scenario propagated a clean DbUpdateException that ErrorMapper.Unwrap maps to the correct Arabic database message. The committed regression test does not cover it, because in a genuine race the winner's row DOES exist at reload time (probe confirms state flips to Unchanged), so only the non-race path reaches the broken branch.
findings.fix: Scope the constraint check to the official-numbers row, as verify-core.json's fix text required, and make the Added entry safe to retry regardless. (a) Pass the row in and require both the extended code and the failing entry: `private static bool IsSequenceRaceException(DbUpdateException exception, OfficialNumber row) => exception is DbUpdateConcurrencyException || (exception.InnerException is SqliteException { SqliteErrorCode: SqliteConstraintErrorCode } sqlite && sqlite.SqliteExtendedErrorCode is SqlitePrimaryKeyConstraint or SqliteUniqueConstraint && exception.Entries.Any(e => ReferenceEquals(e.Entity, row)));` with `private const int SqlitePrimaryKeyConstraint = 1555; private const int SqliteUniqueConstraint = 2067;` — my probe confirms DbUpdateException.Entries carries exactly the offending entry (Other:Added for the unrelated failure, Seq:Added for the real UNIQUE/PK race) and that the real race reports extended code 1555. Update the catch to `catch (DbUpdateException ex) when (IsSequenceRaceException(ex, row))`. (b) Belt-and-braces in the recovery, exactly as verify-core.json prescribed: after `await db.Entry(row).ReloadAsync(...)`, add `if (db.Entry(row).State == EntityState.Added) { db.Entry(row).State = EntityState.Detached; }` before `continue;`, so a still-absent row can never cause the identity conflict on the next iteration. (c) Add a regression test that puts a second, unrelated entity with a violated NOT NULL/FK constraint on the same context alongside a first-ever IssueAsync and asserts that the thrown exception still carries the SqliteException in its InnerException chain (i.e. that it was not misread as a race).

findings.issue: On the exhausted final attempt (lines 186-192) the UserFacingError returned by errorMapper.Map(ex) is thrown away except for its Reference, which is embedded in an English InvalidOperationException message and is recorded nowhere. ErrorMapper.NewReference() mints a fresh random reference on every call, so a caller that maps the escaping exception (ErrorMapper.Unwrap walks InvalidOperationException -> DbUpdateException -> SqliteException) will show the user a DIFFERENT reference from the one in the message — two ids for one failure, which defeats the purpose of a reference. Separately, InvalidOperationException is the same type IssueCoreAsync already uses for the user-actionable refusals (clock check, exhausted sequence, backdated date, no installation), so a caller can no longer tell a business refusal from an infrastructure failure.
findings.fix: Either drop the errorMapper dependency from this path and rethrow the original exception wrapped in a dedicated exception type (e.g. `internal sealed class OfficialNumberRaceException : Exception`) so the caller maps it once and gets one reference, or surface the mapped UserFacingError itself (e.g. an exception type carrying a `UserFacingError Error { get; }` property) instead of only splicing its Reference into an English string. Do not mint a reference that nothing logs.

findings.issue: Issue_WhenAnotherContextInsertedTheVeryFirstRowFirst_IsRetried_AndTheNumbersDiffer covers only the happy branch of the new catch (reload finds the winner's row, entry flips to Unchanged). The retry branch where the reload finds nothing — the branch that actually crashes, see the medium finding — has no test at all, and neither does the exhausted-retry mapping at lines 186-192 (MaxConcurrencyAttempts is unreachable from any test, so the new errorMapper code path is never executed). The 171/171 green run therefore does not demonstrate the finding is fully closed.
findings.fix: Add two tests: (1) the unrelated-constraint test described in the medium finding's fix (c); (2) a test that drives the retry to exhaustion — e.g. keep a pre-tracked Added OfficialNumber and re-add the conflict before each attempt, or make MaxConcurrencyAttempts internal and expose it to the test assembly via InternalsVisibleTo — asserting that what escapes is not a raw DbUpdateException and that its InnerException chain still reaches the SqliteException.

missing_spec_items: verify-core.json finding 1, fix clause 'whose inner SqliteException is SQLITE_CONSTRAINT (error 19) ON OFFICIAL_NUMBERS': the implementation checks only the primary error code and never checks which table/entity failed, so unrelated constraint violations flushed by the same SaveChanges are misclassified as sequence races.

verify-core.json finding 1, fix clause 're-querying (not reloading, since the row was Added: detach it first with db.Entry(row).State = EntityState.Detached)': the builder used a single ReloadAsync for both cases and dropped the detach. This is provably not equivalent — EF Core 10.0.12 leaves an Added entry Added when Reload finds no row (verified) — and the omission is what turns the over-broad catch into an identity-conflict crash.

Spec item 1 'Test with two DbSession contexts over the same file': the new test does open two DbSession contexts over the same file, but the race is staged by pre-tracking an Added entity on the second context rather than by two contexts both taking the 'row is null' branch. The builder's WAL/busy analysis justifying this is credible and the test does exercise the new catch, so this is noted rather than counted as a blocker.

FINDING 1 (OfficialNumberService) — PARTIALLY CLOSED, and it introduced a regression on a neighbouring path. The genuine-race path is correct and the new test is real behaviour, not a tautology: I traced it and it holds — otherSession's pre-tracked Added row makes identity resolution return LastSeq=0 after the winner has committed LastSeq=1, SaveChanges genuinely hits SQLITE_CONSTRAINT on the PK, the new catch reloads to Unchanged/LastSeq=1, and the retry UPDATEs to 2; remove the new catch and the test fails with DbUpdateException. But see the medium finding: because the catch is not scoped to the official-numbers row and the Added entry is not detached, an unrelated constraint failure on any other entity the caller has tracked (the class's own XML doc promises those are flushed by this SaveChanges) is now misread as a race and then crashes on the next iteration with an untranslated EF identity-conflict message, losing the real SqliteException. Both omitted clauses were spelled out in verify-core.json's fix text.

VERIFICATION METHOD for the medium finding (so it is not treated as speculation): I built a throwaway console probe in my scratchpad (C:\Users\abdka\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\D--AI-Administration\f10e20c9-0335-4b7b-9855-1b077265173d\scratchpad\efprobe — outside the repository, nothing in D:\AI\Administration2 touched) against EF Core 10.0.12 + Microsoft.Data.Sqlite with a composite key and an IsConcurrencyToken column mirroring OfficialNumber. Results:
  unrelated failure: type=DbUpdateException code=19 ext=1299 msg=SQLite Error 19: 'NOT NULL constraint failed: Others.Required'.  Entries=Other:Added  -> after Reload, the Seq entry state=Added (NOT detached)  -> re-query returned null  -> second Add THREW InvalidOperationException "The instance of entity type 'Seq' cannot be tracked because another instance with the same key value for {'Kind','Year'} is already being tracked".
  unique race: code=19 ext=1555 msg=SQLite Error 19: 'UNIQUE constraint failed: Seqs.Kind, Seqs.Year'.  Entries=Seq:Added  -> after Reload, state=Unchanged lastSeq=7.
So: IsSequenceRaceException returns true for code 19 ext 1299 today; ex.Entries reliably names the offending entity, making the recommended entity-scoped guard precise; and the extended code cleanly separates the real race (1555/2067) from everything else.
